summary.business_type: Web design & development agency (remote/virtual, US-market-focused; no physical location)
top_findings: Portfolio page presents industry demo templates, not real client work -- zero case studies or testimonials exist anywhere on the site (High, Content & SXO)
No named human authors on any page or blog post -- all content attributed to the Organization only (High, Content)
No detectable backlink profile in Common Crawl; domain is ~2 months old with zero directory/citation presence (High, Off-Page Authority)
Floating mobile contact button overlaps the social-share icon on blog posts -- confirmed real layout bug via DOM overlap detection (High, Visual/UX)
Favicon is 146KB, the single largest network resource on the homepage, loaded on every page site-wide (High, Performance)
quick_wins: Replace the 146KB favicon with a properly optimized icon (a few KB) -- five-minute fix, removes the largest resource on every page
Correct llms.txt, which claims the homepage features 'testimonials' that don't actually exist anywhere on the site
Fix the CSS z-index/position collision between the floating contact button and the share-icon row on mobile blog posts
Switch the site-wide JSON-LD type from ProfessionalService to Organization + ContactPoint (ready-made snippet in findings/schema.md) -- resolves the LocalBusiness-without-address mismatch
Add /privacy and /terms to sitemap.xml, and replace the shared build-time lastmod on 11 static pages with real per-page dates
Increase mobile nav icon tap targets (theme toggle, hamburger) from 32x32px to at least 44x44px

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: All 32 sitemap URLs return clean 200s with self-referencing canonicals, no duplicate titles
Correct domain canonicalization (non-www and http both 308-redirect to https://www.)
True HTTP 404 on nonexistent pages; consistent index,follow meta robots sitewide
Strong, consistent security headers (CSP, HSTS w/ preload, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) on homepage AND interior pages
Fully server-rendered content, crawlable without JS execution
llms.txt present at root with a clean page manifest

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for script-src and style-src
findings.description: Reduces the XSS-mitigation value of the Content-Security-Policy header.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to nonce- or hash-based CSP via Next.js middleware.

findings.title: llms.txt uses apex (non-www) URLs requiring a redirect hop
findings.description: Links 308-redirect from pinexadigital.com to www.pinexadigital.com.
findings.recommendation: Update llms.txt to use canonical www URLs directly.

findings.title: No IndexNow integration
findings.description: No IndexNow key file or publish-time ping despite regular blog publishing.
findings.recommendation: Add IndexNow key and ping on publish/update for faster Bing/Yandex pickup.

findings.title: Sitemap lastmod is a shared build timestamp for static pages
findings.description: 11 non-blog URLs share one identical lastmod value that tracks build time, not content changes.
findings.recommendation: Only update lastmod on genuine content change.

findings.title: /privacy and /terms exist but are missing from the sitemap
findings.description: Both return HTTP 200 and are crawlable but absent from sitemap.xml.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether intentional; if not, add both with low priority.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Differentiated, non-boilerplate service page copy across all 4 service pages
Specific, checkable claims (pricing, PageSpeed scores, delivery timelines) instead of vague marketing language
Blog content structured for direct-answer extraction (numbered lists, decision tables, good-sign/red-flag framing)
Consistent, opinionated brand voice reading as domain-expert-written, not templated filler
Honest FAQ content addressing real objections on /pricing and service pages

findings.title: No named human authors anywhere on the site
findings.description: BlogPosting.author and all bylines use Organization type only, never Person, across every sampled page.
findings.recommendation: Add named author(s) with title/bio to blog posts; set BlogPosting.author to Person.

findings.title: Portfolio shows demo templates, not real client work -- no case studies or testimonials exist
findings.description: /portfolio explicitly presents 8 industry demo templates ('imagine your brand in its place'); no other page has client names, testimonials, or outcome data.
findings.recommendation: Add a real case-study section as client projects ship.

findings.title: About page makes unverified experience claims
findings.description: /about asserts process maturity without concrete numbers (years operating, project count, team size).
findings.recommendation: Add specific, verifiable proof points to /about.

findings.title: Process description duplicated near-verbatim between /about and /services/web-design
findings.description: The Discovery/Design/Build narrative repeats in very similar phrasing on both pages.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate tone/detail level between the two instances.

categories.name: On-Page SEO (Search Experience)
what_works: Pricing and e-commerce pages closely match the trust-building/comparison format Google rewards for their query types
Service pages name specific tools/tech as credible expertise signals rather than generic claims
Blog posts open with direct, quotable answers and use original frameworks
Consistent 'who this is for' segmentation across service pages qualifies visitors efficiently

findings.title: Portfolio page structurally mismatches its search intent
findings.description: Visitors expecting real client proof instead find industry demo templates.
findings.recommendation: Add a real case-study section as client work accumulates.

findings.title: Homepage lacks above-fold social proof
findings.description: Homepage answers relevance well but not trust within the first scroll.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact trust strip once real client data exists.

findings.title: E-commerce service page and two blog posts overlap in message and audience
findings.description: Three pages answer the same Shopify-vs-WooCommerce decision with inconsistent depth and no cross-linking.
findings.recommendation: Cross-link the service page and blog posts explicitly.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: Site-wide JSON-LD @graph (WebSite + ProfessionalService) injected identically via root layout, correct @id linking
Prior Critical finding resolved: self-authored AggregateRating/Review block fully removed
BreadcrumbList correctly implemented on every non-homepage page
Service schema on all 4 service sub-pages with correct Offer/pricing presence
/pricing uses ItemList of Offer for all 3 tiers; Blog/BlogPosting complete with image, dates, author, publisher
FAQPage markup present and verified to match visible content; no deprecated schema types anywhere

findings.title: ProfessionalService (LocalBusiness subtype) used for a remote agency with no address
findings.description: Implies a physical location Google's guidance assumes for LocalBusiness types; compounded by an Indian phone number vs. US areaServed.
findings.recommendation: Switch to Organization + ContactPoint (ready-made JSON-LD in findings/schema.md).

findings.title: Service.provider duplicates organization data instead of referencing the shared @id
findings.description: Each Service block re-declares an inline provider object instead of an @id reference.
findings.recommendation: Replace inline provider with an @id reference to the canonical org node.

findings.title: Portfolio page has no item-level schema for the 8 demo showcases
findings.description: No ItemList/CreativeWork markup for the individual demo tiles.
findings.recommendation: Add an ItemList of CreativeWork entries.

findings.title: sameAs LinkedIn link returned an inconclusive automated status (HTTP 999)
findings.description: LinkedIn's standard anti-bot response; inconclusive, not confirmed broken.
findings.recommendation: Manually verify; consider a Company Page instead of a personal profile URL.

categories.name: Performance (Core Web Vitals)
what_works: Desktop performance excellent: Lighthouse 100/100, LCP 0.7s
CLS is 0 (perfect) across every page and viewport tested
TBT is low everywhere (58-80ms), well within the good threshold
Reasonable total page weight (~649KB, 32 requests) with responsive/lazy-loaded images and font preloading already in place

findings.title: Favicon is 146KB, the largest resource on the homepage
findings.description: /favicon.png transfers 146,954 bytes, larger than the hero image, loaded on every page site-wide.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a properly optimized favicon (a few KB).

findings.title: Mobile LCP in the Needs Improvement band on all pages tested
findings.description: Lab LCP under mobile throttling ranges 2.9-3.9s across 4 pages tested, versus a <2.5s Good threshold.
findings.recommendation: Identify and prioritize the actual LCP element per page (fetchpriority=high, reduce JS-hydration blocking).

findings.title: Multiple 40-70KB JS chunks load on the homepage
findings.description: Several Next.js chunk files compete with the LCP element for mobile bandwidth/parse time.
findings.recommendation: Code-split non-critical sections to load after first paint.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: robots.txt fully open, no AI crawler blocked
Well-formed llms.txt with page manifest and explicit AI citation/attribution policy
Blog content structured for direct extraction (numbered frameworks, direct answers)
FAQPage schema present and verified to match visible content
All structured data server-rendered, fully visible without JS execution

findings.title: llms.txt claims testimonials exist on the homepage -- they don't
findings.description: llms.txt Home entry mentions 'testimonials' but none exist anywhere on the site.
findings.recommendation: Add real testimonials or correct the llms.txt description.

findings.title: No explicit per-bot rules in robots.txt
findings.description: Blanket Allow: / works but provides no auditable, bot-specific confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add explicit User-agent blocks for major AI crawlers.

findings.title: Thin brand-entity disambiguation signals
findings.description: sameAs only links LinkedIn and Instagram; no Crunchbase/Clutch/G2/Wikidata presence.
findings.recommendation: Claim agency-directory profiles as both backlinks and sameAs signals.

categories.name: Images / Visual UX
what_works: Homepage above-the-fold: H1, sub-headline, and two CTAs fully visible without scrolling on desktop and mobile
No horizontal scroll, no broken/unsized images, no console errors across all 12 page/viewport combinations tested
All homepage images have descriptive, non-generic alt text; consistent 16px readable typography sitewide
Contact page desktop layout shows the full lead-capture form above the fold

findings.title: Floating contact button overlaps social-share icon on mobile blog post
findings.description: Confirmed via DOM overlap detector: a real layout collision on the mobile blog post, not a screenshot artifact.
findings.recommendation: Add position-aware logic so floating buttons don't render over other interactive elements.

findings.title: Large empty vertical gap between header and content on every interior page
findings.description: Substantial blank space pushes content and CTAs out of the above-the-fold area, especially on mobile.
findings.recommendation: Reduce top padding/margin on interior page hero sections.

findings.title: Contact form not visible above the fold on mobile
findings.description: Mobile stacks trust bullets above the form, pushing it to top:1442px, far below the 812px viewport.
findings.recommendation: Reorder or compress the mobile stack so the form appears sooner.

findings.title: Mobile nav icon buttons below recommended tap-target size
findings.description: Theme-toggle and hamburger buttons measure 32x32px, below the 44-48px recommended minimum.
findings.recommendation: Increase tappable hit area to at least 44x44px.

supplementary.name: Off-Page Authority / Backlinks
supplementary.confidence: Low -- Tier 0 (Common Crawl only), directional floor score, not a confidence-weighted assessment
supplementary.note: Not included in the weighted health score; the seo-audit skill's category weights don't allocate a slot for backlinks. Domain is genuinely new (~2 months old, registered 2026-06-21) with zero detectable backlinks -- expected at this stage, not a defect.

findings.title: Zero referring domains / no backlink authority signal exists
findings.description: Forced re-download of Common Crawl's web graph confirms the domain remains entirely absent from the crawl.
findings.recommendation: Expected for a new domain; begin structured outreach now that indexability is fixed.

findings.title: No directory or citation presence yet
findings.description: No Google Business Profile, Clutch, DesignRush, or GoodFirms listing found.
findings.recommendation: List on Clutch, DesignRush, GoodFirms, and Google Business Profile -- free, high-authority, industry-relevant.

supplementary.name: Blog Content Architecture
supplementary.note: Qualitative content-cluster analysis feeding into the Content Quality and On-Page categories' quick wins; not independently scored.

findings.title: Confirmed cannibalization: two 'Shopify vs WooCommerce' posts target the same query space
findings.description: Same core keyword, same intent, one-directional linking between the two.
findings.recommendation: Pick one as canonical, or re-scope the older post around a distinctly different query.

findings.title: SEO/AI-search content cluster (4 posts) has no corresponding service page to convert into
findings.description: The second-largest topical cluster on the blog funnels only to a generic /services or /contact.
findings.recommendation: Add an SEO/AEO line item to /services, or fold explicitly into /services/web-design.

findings.title: Internal linking from posts to service/pricing pages is thin and inconsistent
findings.description: 5 of 6 audited posts have exactly one manually-placed contextual link; 'Related articles' modules appear recency-based, not topic-aware.
findings.recommendation: Add contextual spoke-to-spoke links; make related-articles topic-aware.

phases.name: Phase 1: Quick Wins
items: Replace the 146KB favicon with a properly optimized icon (Performance, High)
Fix the mobile floating-button/share-icon CSS collision on blog posts (Visual, High)
Correct llms.txt's inaccurate 'testimonials' claim (GEO, Medium)
Switch site-wide schema from ProfessionalService to Organization + ContactPoint using the ready-made snippet (Schema, Medium)
Add /privacy and /terms to sitemap.xml; fix static-page lastmod dates (Technical/Sitemap, Medium)
Increase mobile nav tap targets to 44x44px (Visual, Medium)

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Reduce header-to-content whitespace on interior pages, especially mobile (Visual, Medium)
Reorder the mobile Contact page so the form appears above the fold (Visual, Medium)
Resolve the Shopify-vs-WooCommerce content cannibalization -- consolidate or re-scope (Content Architecture, High)
Add contextual internal links between blog posts and relevant service pages (Content Architecture, Medium)
Harden CSP by removing 'unsafe-inline' via nonce-based script/style policy (Technical, Medium)
Investigate and improve mobile LCP timing across key pages (Performance, Medium)

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Add named human author(s) with bio/credentials to blog content and BlogPosting schema (Content, High)
Build a real case-study section as client projects ship, replacing/supplementing the demo showcase (Content & SXO, High)
Add verifiable proof points to /about (years operating, project count, team size) (Content, Medium)
Claim directory listings on Clutch, DesignRush, GoodFirms, and Google Business Profile (Off-Page, High)
Add an SEO/AI-search service page or fold that content cluster into an existing service page (Content Architecture, Medium)

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Add IndexNow integration for faster Bing/Yandex pickup on new blog posts
Configure Moz free tier once directory listings/guest posts go live to track referring domains as the backlink profile grows
Re-run a full audit after Phase 1-2 items ship to confirm fixes and re-baseline scores
Monitor mobile LCP via real CrUX field data once Google API credentials are configured
